result.topic_en: Euler lists, for a = 3, 5, 6, the residue classes of n for which 4n±1 divides x²±ay² and a^{2n}±1 or a^{2n-1}±1; he notes anomalies when a is composite or n is even, and explains them by the divisibility of (ab)^x − 1. He then states the unproved theorem that a^m − 1 is divisible by the prime 2m+1 = 4ab ± ii.

methods.what: Classification for a=3 of primes 4n±1 dividing x²±3y² and 3^{2n}∓1 or 3^{2n-1}∓1 by n mod 3
methods.quote: pro I. $n=3p+0$, vel $3p+2$, ideoque $4n+1=12p+1$, $12p+9$, ubi casus posterior est rejiciendus, ita, ut sit $4n+1=12p+1$, per quem divisibiles sunt $x^2\pm3y^2$ et $3^{2n}-1$;

methods.what: Same classification for a=5 by n mod 5
Same classification for a=6 by n mod 6
Correction of the residues r for even or composite a (example a=10) by dividing the numbers 0, 2, 6, 12, 20, ... by 2
methods.quote: Ita si $a=10$, primo pro $r$ reperimus hos valores 0, 2, 6; per binarium autem dividendo insuper accedunt ad $r$ 1, 3, ita, ut valores ipsius $r$ jam sint 0, 1, 2, 3, 6

methods.what: If a^x−1 and b^x−1 are divisible by the prime 2x+1, so is (ab)^x−1
methods.quote: si enim $a^x-1$ est divisibile, erit etiam $(ab)^x-b^x$; addatur formula divisibilis $b^x-1$, prodit formula divisibilis $(ab)^x-1$

methods.what: If a^x+1 and b^x+1 are divisible by 2x+1, then (ab)^x−1 is divisible
methods.quote: cum enim ex priori sequatur $(ab)^x+b^x$ divisibilis, auferendo hinc $b^x+1$ remanet $(ab)^x-1$ divisibilis

methods.what: Criterion: if the prime 2m+1 = 4ab ± i², then ±a (or +a) is a quadratic residue and a^m − 1 is divisible by 2m+1
methods.quote: utroque autem casu, hoc est si $2m+1=4ab\pm ii$, formulam $a^m-1$ divisibilem esse per $2m+1$

items.quote: si fuerit $2m+1=4ab+ii$ (denotante $i$ numeros impares), tum in residuis quadratorum tam $+a$ quam $-a$ reperiri; sin autem fuerit $2m+1=4ab-ii$, tum tantum $+a$ in residuis occurrere; utroque autem casu, hoc est si $2m+1=4ab\pm ii$, formulam $a^m-1$ divisibilem esse per $2m+1$. Hujus quidem demonstratio nondum perfecta habetur
items.english: If 2m+1 = 4ab + i² (i odd), then both +a and −a are found among the quadratic residues; if 2m+1 = 4ab − i², only +a occurs. In either case, i.e. if 2m+1 = 4ab ± i², the formula a^m − 1 is divisible by 2m+1. A perfect proof of this is not yet had.

items.quote: Totum igitur hoc argumentum accuratius sequenti modo simulque concinnius pertractatur.
items.english: This whole argument is therefore treated more accurately, and at the same time more neatly, in the following way.
